bug_semantics: tapslip6's devopen() builds a device path in a 1024-byte stack buffer by strcpy(t, "/dev/") then strcat(t, dev) with no length check. The -s option stores the caller-supplied serial device name (optarg, or optarg+5 if it already starts with "/dev/") in siodev and later passes that pointer to devopen(); an overlong -s value overflows t on strcat, matching the Seclists/ASan PoC (WRITE of size 3001 into the stack frame). Impact is local stack memory corruption / crash of the host-side SLIP helper (CWE-121). The same unbounded strcpy/strcat pair was still present at 2026.01-devel-317 (66a6eab997).
flaw_origin: The unbounded strcpy/strcat path was first written in RIOT when Martine Lenders imported the Contiki tunslip tools. Commit 1a146f7934d02324361b90980243286b3db432e3 added dist/tools/tunslip/tapslip6.c as a new file whose original devopen() (lines 416-423) is exactly char t[1024]; strcpy(t, "/dev/"); strcat(t, dev); return open(t, flags); and whose main() -s handler (siodev = optarg / optarg+5, then slipfd = devopen(siodev, ...)) is the attack entry. git log -L on that function shows no later rewrite of the sink before the 2026 bounds check; blame at the fix parent still names 1a146f79. Parent d2fea78e76 has no dist/tools/tunslip/tapslip6.c. The import is a single-parent, non-merge, non-squash first-write in this repo (later carried by merge 1d74a730 of PR #2688).
